chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Hearing King Oliver's band at the Savoy, with Red Allen
summary: Oliver fronted his Savoy band without playing while Red Allen did the trumpet work, and the band broke up and mostly returned to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: ...when lots of bands were coming in and out of New York.
And you also remember hearing King Oliver.

Yeah, I heard him. I heard him at the Savoy Ballroom. What attracted me to the band was the fact that King Oliver didn't play anything. He was in front of the band as a director, but he didn't play no trumpet. He didn't play trumpet at all. And Red Allen was in the band doing all the trumpet work -- the featured trumpeter. And who else was in the band that I knew...?
So that was the first time you heard Henry Allen?
That was the first time I'd heard of him

even. I hadn't even heard of him before. And I didn't know him or anything like that... But he was standing up in featured in the band, he did all the trumpet work. And I expected to hear King Oliver play, but he wasn't playing. His teeth were bad or something -- he was having trouble.

Barney Bigard was in the band -- the tenor player, clarinet. And Omar Simeon was in the band. I forget what the tenor player's name was. There was another saxophone man. Anyway, I didn't know too many of the members of the band. Paul Barbarin was the drummer.
But they didn't stay around New York. They finished their engagement at the Savoy, and the band got into some hard times. And the majority of them went back to Chicago.
